meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and when?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in class against a weekend with the play open on his desk. Of course he cited lines. You still haven't told me who decided.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then show me the version history. And for the third time, who decided?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that the checker score proves nothing on its own and took it off the table. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology, a straight answer about who decided on the zero, and the version history in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, an answer about who decided, and to see the version history. The fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, but the meeting ended before any evidence was on the table.
What moved her: Nothing; your writing comparison was specific and dated, but she had an easy answer to it (a timed class piece against a weekend essay with the play open), and you named the version history without showing it.
What cost ground: You never answered who decided on the zero, even though she asked three times, and procedure is the ground she fights on most comfortably.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence didn't get near that night, because you mentioned the version history but gave no times from it; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: In your first reply, answer who decided and own that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put the version history's dates and times in front of her the moment you mention it.
